simple: **Money** is anything most sellers will accept for real goods: a **generally acceptable medium of exchange (GA-MOE)**. It runs on **trust**; law only enforces acceptance.
Modern money is a **promise issued by the RBI**, backed by a promise from the government (**bonds**). The RBI earns **seigniorage** because its liabilities cost almost nothing.
**Money supply = m x M0**. The RBI makes the base (M0); banks multiply it. More cash preference (**cdr**) or more reserves (**rdr**) shrinks the multiplier.
The **cost of money** (interest rate) comes from a **vertical supply curve** meeting a downward-sloping demand curve. At **r-min** a **liquidity trap** switches policy off.
RBI uses **qualitative** tools (nudges) and **quantitative** tools (OMO, CRR, SLR, repo, reverse repo, MSF, SDF). The **corridor** is MSF (ceiling), repo, SDF (floor).
**FIT 2015** fixes the goal at **4% +/- 2%**, set by a **6-member MPC**. Loan pricing moved **PLR, Base Rate, MCLR, EBLR** to improve transmission.
terms: GA-MOE
Generally acceptable medium of exchange: the definition of money.
Double Coincidence of Wants (DCW)
In barter you must find someone who has what you want and wants what you have.
Legal tender
A way of settling debt that a creditor cannot lawfully refuse; in India notes, coins and CBDC.
Representative money
Paper promises backed 1:1 by gold held in a vault.
Fiat money
Central bank promises backed by government bonds; the rupee is not a claim on gold.
Seigniorage
Net interest income on assets backing the currency, after printing costs.
High-powered money (M0)
Currency notes created by the central bank; the RBI's total liabilities.
Narrow and broad money
M1 and M2 are narrow; M3 and M4 are broad.
Money multiplier (m)
How much banks multiply M0 into total money supply: MS = m x M0.
cdr and rdr
Currency-deposit ratio and reserve-deposit ratio; the higher each is, the lower m.
Velocity (v)
How many times a unit of money changes hands in a period.
Liquidity trap
At r-min everyone holds cash, so more money supply does not lower rates or raise spending.
NDTL
Net demand and time liabilities: demand and time deposits less inter-bank deposits.
Monetary transmission
Whether banks pass RBI's rate decisions on to the real economy.
Sterilisation
Absorbing the rupees created by buying dollars; the MSS does this.
MIBOR
Mumbai Inter-bank Offered Rate; the standard call rate in the inter-bank market.
8.remember: Money is trust. RBI makes the base, banks multiply it, and the tools and the corridor set what it costs.

traps.d: Legal tender laws do not create value; they only enforce acceptance for settling a debt.
traps.r: Rule: value comes from trust; legal tender gives enforced acceptance, not value.

traps.d: Vault cash with banks, inter-bank deposits and the Government of India's deposits with RBI are not counted.
traps.r: Rule: MS measures what the public holds; if an option counts vault cash or government deposits, reject it.

traps.d: In repo the RBI lends to banks; in reverse repo the RBI borrows from banks when liquidity is in surplus.
traps.r: Rule: repo = RBI lends (1 to 14 days); reverse repo = RBI borrows.

traps.t: The floor is now the SDF
traps.d: The floor was earlier the reverse repo; since April 2022 the SDF is the hard floor, set just below the repo.
traps.r: Rule: ceiling MSF, benchmark repo, floor SDF.

traps.d: The RBI Amendment Act of 2006 removed the 3% floor and the 40% ceiling on CRR.
traps.r: Rule: CRR can be set anywhere from 0% to 100%; CRR is cash with RBI earning nothing, SLR is gold and bonds.

traps.d: The handout writes all three as f(marginal cost of funds), but Base Rate and MCLR are internal while EBLR is external.
traps.r: Rule: Base Rate 2010, MCLR 2016, EBLR 2019; only EBLR is linked to an outside rate.
